seed: Three lines drawn end to end are a triangle, not three lines in a bag. This walk draws three, picks all three rows, turns them into a path from the row menu, and checks that ONE closed path of three corners comes back where the three lines were, that the question said so first, that the shape can be reshaped afterwards, and that one undo puts the three lines back.

steps.note: three separate line layers drawn end to end. They LOOK like a triangle and are nothing of the kind: three rows in the layers list, no inside, nothing to fill
the row menu opened on one of three picked rows still offers 'Turn Into Path…', and it is about all three

THE POINT OF THE QUESTION: it reads 'Turn these 3 shapes into one path?' and says their ends meet, so they join into one outline, that it comes back to where it started so it closes and you can paint inside it, and that undo puts it back. Nothing has changed yet

THE POINT: one layer, one closed outline of three corners, sitting exactly where the three lines were. Compare doc-1-three-lines with doc-4-one-path: the picture is the same triangle. The row is called Path, because 'Line 3' is a poor name for a triangle

the top corner was picked up and pulled, and the two runs either side came with it. Three lines could never have done this together. The corner is point 1 of the joined outline, not point 0: the outline starts at the shape whose row the menu was opened on, which is the same shape whose look the path keeps
one undo puts the corner back, the second takes the whole join back to three separate lines: joining three shapes is ONE step, not three. Compare doc-6-lines-back with doc-1-three-lines

THE OTHER HALF OF THE PROMISE: a line away on its own picked with the triangle. The question says no two of their ends are within 2 pt of each other, so they stay separate outlines. The tolerance is a number you are told, not one you have to guess
